concept: Facts about one thing as term and detail pairs in a real dl, stacked or in two columns that stack again when narrow.

default_to_avoid.pattern: a description list drawn as a table with bold labels and borders on every cell
default_to_avoid.kind: description list, key value list, properties, details
default_to_avoid.why_not: a bordered grid shouts its structure and a table is the wrong element for pairs; Pane uses tones and space and a dl

derivation.consequence: secondary text keeps the lowest opacity that still measured as passing; text halos count only where WCAG allows them
derivation.form: terms take the label size in the secondary tone and details the body size in the primary tone

derivation.consequence: padding inside a pane is larger than the gap between items in it, so the edge reads as the object's boundary
derivation.form: pairs are separated by space, and hairlines only appear when a long list asks for them

derivation.consequence: light falls from above, so every surface carries a rim brightest along its top edge and a soft shadow below that says where it floats, and a recess is the inverse, shaded under its top lip and lit on its bottom lip; a nested surface adds no second blur, because one sheet of glass is one layer
derivation.form: it adds no pane of its own and sits on the card or the sheet it describes

variants.reason: A tells term from detail by tone and size (P2). B adds borders on every cell. C puts label colons in front of every value.

root.why: the pairs stack with an even gap and the list measures its own width for the layout

pair.why: each term and its detail are grouped so they move together when the layout changes

term.why: the term is secondary at label size so the detail is what the eye reads

detail.why: the detail is primary at body size and wraps anywhere so long values never spill

inline.why: inline layout puts terms in their own column and stacks again in a narrow pane

dividers.why: dividers draw a hairline between pairs for long lists such as an order summary
